key.label: Four Choc Keys · R23
key.note: Choc V1 openings retain their 14.1 mm square seats with 0.2 mm corner rounding. The outer shoulders are deliberately curved; the openings must not narrow after printing.

steps.title: Snip Off the Print Pads
steps.caption: With the part cool, snip across the exposed middle of each narrow tie. Keep the cutter away from the permanent holder and clear the wire openings.

steps.title: Solder the Sockets Off the Holder
steps.caption: With the holder off the rod and upside down on the bench, solder each socket's two wires outside the holder. Keep solder on the terminal tabs, not above them.

steps.title: Slide In the Lower-Left Socket
steps.caption: Hold the socket about 2 mm below its seat and slide it in from the left edge, above the thin guard runners, wires trailing outward. Under its seat, lift it straight up so the two bosses enter the backplate.

steps.title: Slide In the Lower-Right Socket
steps.caption: Hold the socket about 2 mm below its seat and slide it in from the right edge, above the thin guard runners, wires trailing outward. Under its seat, lift it straight up so the two bosses enter the backplate.

steps.title: Push Up the Upper Sockets
steps.caption: Bring each socket up about 1 mm away from the rod position, so its inner solder joint passes beside the ring arm. 2 mm below the seat, move it in and press it up.

steps.title: Tape Every Socket
steps.caption: Lay one strip of polyimide tape across each socket and its wires onto the backplate, as on R16. Press the tape ends onto the backplate with a flat tool. Keep pressure off the guard runners. The tape insulates the solder from the rod and holds the socket.

steps.title: Press In the Switches
steps.caption: Back each socket from below with a finger or flat tool, then press each switch in from above until it clicks into the plate.

steps.title: Slide Onto the Rod
steps.caption: Slide the wired holder onto the rod end-first. The rod runs through the two rings behind the lower row; the guard has no ring of its own.

steps.title: Seated
steps.caption: Final position. The index finger rests on the rod between the inner runners; the runners sit under the lower sockets' outer terminals.

steps.title: Remove Print Supports
steps.caption: Cut the pad ties. Clear supports from the OP1 board slot, the plug opening and lead groove underneath, and both hinge holes. Check that the bracket arms flex freely and both post clips are clean.

steps.title: Lower the OP1 Board
steps.caption: With the holder off the rod, lower the board onto its two seats at its 25° angle. Its switch end sits under the three-key row; the keys can stay fitted.

steps.title: Secure the Board
steps.caption: Fit the two kit screws through the eyelets. Tighten gently until the board stops moving.

steps.title: Connect the Harness Underneath
steps.caption: From below, push the plug up into the white socket. Press its lead into the open groove beside the rod channel so it leaves at the two-key end. Do this before the holder goes on the rod.

steps.title: Seat the Mouse Switch
steps.caption: Seat the mouse switch in its three socket barrels. Keep all three pins straight.

steps.title: Slide the Holder onto the Rod
steps.caption: Slide the wired holder onto the rod. The plug and lead stay beside the rod channel; do not pull on the lead.

steps.title: Bring the Bracket Over the Supports
steps.caption: Bring the orange bracket above the two fixed supports. The side arms and their pins are part of the bracket.

steps.title: Set the OP1 Stop Screw
steps.caption: Fit the M2 × 4 stop screw head-down into the bracket boss. Screw it fully in, then back it out about one turn.

steps.title: Pinch the Bracket Arms
steps.caption: Pinch the side arms just enough for their pins to clear the supports. Do not force them past the centre stop.

steps.title: Lower Between the Supports
steps.caption: Keep the arms pinched and lower the bracket between the supports.

steps.title: Let the Tabs Snap Into the Holes
steps.caption: Release the arms so both pins enter the support holes. Check both sides are retained.

steps.title: Plug In and Fit the Board
steps.caption: Plug the Gravity lead into the board, then lower the board over both posts with the gold pad at the three-key end.

steps.title: Clip the Posts
steps.caption: Slide each printed clip onto its post neck from the three-key end until it snaps. The clips hold the board down.

steps.title: Touch, Click and Release
steps.caption: Press the gold pad. The bracket pivots onto the OP1 switch under the three-key row. Check that it clicks, stops on the screw and returns freely. This is a nominal CAD stop, not a promised click.

steps.title: Pull Off the Clips
steps.caption: To adjust or remove the board, slide both clips off towards the three-key end.

steps.title: Lift the Board Off the Posts
steps.caption: Lift the board straight up off the posts with its lead attached.

steps.title: Pinch to Release the Tabs
steps.caption: Pinch the side arms until both pins leave the support holes.

steps.title: Lift Off the Bracket
steps.caption: Lift the bracket out with the stop screw.

steps.title: Adjust the Stop Screw
steps.caption: If it did not click, turn the screw in a quarter turn for more travel. If it pressed hard after the click, turn it out a quarter turn.

steps.title: Pinch and Lower It Back
steps.caption: Keep the arms pinched and lower the bracket between the supports.

steps.title: Let the Tabs Snap Back In
steps.caption: Release the arms so both pins snap back into the holes.

steps.title: Fit the Board Back on the Posts
steps.caption: Lower the board over both posts without trapping its lead.

steps.title: Refit the Clips
steps.caption: Slide both clips back onto the post necks until they snap.

steps.title: Check the Click Again
steps.caption: Press the pad again. It should click before the stop and spring back fully.

steps.title: Pinch the Bracket Arms
steps.caption: Hold the orange bracket above the holder. Pinch the two raised pads under the connector end so both tabs pull inwards.

steps.title: Lower Between the Supports
steps.caption: Keep pinching and lower the bracket. The two tabs pass between the two fixed supports.

steps.title: Let the Tabs Snap Into the Holes
steps.caption: Let go. Each arm springs back and its tab enters the hole in the support beside it.

steps.title: Pinch to Release the Tabs
steps.caption: Pinch both pads. The tabs pull out of the support holes.

steps.title: Lift Off the Empty Bracket
steps.caption: Keep pinching and lift the bracket straight up.

steps.title: Pinch and Lower It Back
steps.caption: To refit, pinch again and lower the bracket between the supports.

steps.title: Let the Tabs Snap Back In
steps.caption: Let go so both tabs return into their holes.

snap_hinge.note: The whole orange bracket from the full assembly, with the key holder cut away round the supports. Pinch the arms to fit or remove it.

xiao.label: XIAO holder · R25 lift-release trial
xiao.note: Fit the R25 holder and keeper together to try the stronger catch. The board sits in its original position. Keep the USB-C socket, reset button and antenna end accessible. The keeper belongs to this XIAO holder, not the battery.

keeper.label: R25 keeper and rounded lift tab

steps.title: Snip Off the Print Pads
steps.caption: With the part cool, snip across the exposed middle of each narrow tie. Keep the cutter away from the permanent holder and clear the wire openings.

steps.title: Lay In the Board
steps.caption: Tilt the near end of the board up about 6 degrees, slide the USB end under the two far fingers, then lower the near end onto its ledges. Side wires stay outside the walls. Underside solder must leave room: see the clearance map in geometry-checks.json.

steps.title: Point the Tooth Toward the Holder
steps.caption: Line up the two side ears with the grooves. The small tooth faces down and the rounded edge faces the board.

steps.title: Slide On the Keeper
steps.caption: Push along the grooves until the tab drops behind the ridge. The prongs rest over the two corners of the board.

steps.title: Slide the Rod Through the Rings
steps.caption: Feed the rod through both rings, end-first.

steps.title: Pull Gently to Check the Stop
steps.caption: A small straight pull brings the tooth against the steep face. The board prongs stay flat.

steps.title: Lift the Rounded Tab
steps.caption: Lift the rounded edge a little with a fingernail. The tooth rises above the ridge.

steps.title: Slide the Keeper Out
steps.caption: Keep the tab raised while you slide the keeper back along its two grooves.

steps.title: Let the Tab Settle
steps.caption: Let go once the tooth is clear. The spring tab returns to its flat shape.

steps.title: Lift the Board Out
steps.caption: Lift the keeper end of the board and slide the USB end out from under the far fingers.

steps.title: Slide the Holder Off the Rod
steps.caption: Draw the rod out through the rings to separate the holder.

xiao_latch.label: XIAO keeper latch · R25 cutaway
xiao_latch.note: Side section of the matching R25 parts. The bend is drawn from the checked CAD route.

holder.label: Blue holder ridge and steep face

keeper.label: Orange keeper tooth and spring tab

steps.title: Find the Ramp and Tooth
steps.caption: The orange spring is joined to the keeper outside this side section. The blue ridge has a slope on the way in and a steep face on the way out.

steps.title: Push Until It Clicks
steps.caption: The tooth climbs the blue slope. The tab drops flat once the tooth passes the steep face.

steps.title: Pull Gently to Check the Stop
steps.caption: A small straight pull brings the tooth against the steep face. The board prongs stay flat.

steps.title: Lift the Rounded Tab
steps.caption: Lift the rounded edge a little with a fingernail. The tooth rises above the ridge.

steps.title: Slide the Keeper Out
steps.caption: Keep the tab raised while you slide the keeper back along its two grooves.

steps.title: Let the Tab Settle
steps.caption: Let go once the tooth is clear. The spring tab returns to its flat shape.

battery.label: Battery holder · lower click-in door
battery.note: The existing LP402025 envelope is shown. A replacement cell must be checked before use.

door.label: Battery end door · press tab to release

steps.title: Clear the Print Pads
steps.caption: Snip the narrow pad ties once cool. Clear the two door slots; the battery door is the wide plate with one central spring tab.

steps.title: Slide the Battery In
steps.caption: Slide the non-wire end in first. Keep both wires through the middle opening; never force or squeeze the pouch.

steps.title: Press the Door Tab
steps.caption: Press the rounded central tab away from the battery. This bends only its spring, clearing the catch.

steps.title: Slide Down Both Door Edges
steps.caption: Keep the tab pressed and lower both side edges through the two grooves until the door reaches its bottom stop.

steps.title: Let the Catch Engage
steps.caption: Release the tab. Its tooth moves under the holder lip. Check that the door stays down with a gentle lift.

steps.title: Slide Onto the Rod
steps.caption: Slide the assembled holder onto an accessible rod end.

steps.title: Battery Held in Place
steps.caption: The sides guide the door; the middle tooth keeps it from lifting. This is a CAD fit trial, not measured retention force.

steps.title: Release the Battery Door
steps.caption: Press the small tab away from the battery to clear the lip. Do not pull hard on a latched door.

steps.title: Lift the Door Out
steps.caption: Hold the tab pressed and lift the wide door straight up its side grooves.

steps.title: Release the Tab
steps.caption: Once out of the grooves, let the spring return to its flat shape.

steps.title: Remove the Battery
steps.caption: Withdraw the battery by its body, keeping the wires clear of the opening.

steps.title: Slide the Holder Off
steps.caption: With an accessible rod end, slide the empty holder off.
